text:
maya: customer reported 403 on every request after seat upgrade this morning. billing UI shows new seats, customer still blocked. logs attached below.

maya: curl reproducer they used:
```
curl -H \"Authorization: ApiKey cust_XXXX\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}' -v
> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
> content-type: application/json
{"error":"access_denied","reason":"plan_gate"}
```

maya: they see error body with \"reason: plan_gate\" but front-end shows \"invalid api key\" sometimes. asking if plan checks are being surfaced as auth. any quick triage steps?

arjun: likely a plan/entitlement gating path, not auth. two common causes: 1) billing-to-entitlement sync lag, 2) stale tenant entitlement cache. do we have tenant_id and api key?

maya: tenant_id t-78b9, api key sent in DM. billing team confirms upgrade processed at 08:17 UTC. customer called at 08:30 and still 403.

zach: billing confirmed the invoice/seat change completed. our internal entitlement store shows new plan but cache node still served old TTL at 08:29 in the logs.

arjun: can you paste the exact log line from the runtime? look for `plan_check` tag.

maya: here's the runtime trace (redacted):
```
[2026-03-17T08:29:12Z] request_id=xyz plan_check:start tenant=t-78b9 api_key=cust_XXXX
[2026-03-17T08:29:12Z] entitlement_cache: miss key=tenant:t-78b9
[2026-03-17T08:29:12Z] entitlement_sync: last_sync=2026-03-17T07:50:01Z
[2026-03-17T08:29:12Z] plan_check: FAIL reason=plan_gate code=403
```

arjun: yep, that's cache miss + stale sync window. two quick fixes: 1) force-clear tenant entitlement cache for t-78b9, 2) kick off a sync job for that tenant. both are admin ops.

arjun: admin command (internal):
```
POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/t-78b9/cache/clear
Headers: X-Admin-Token: $ADMIN_TOKEN
```

arjun: and to trigger a sync:
```
POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/t-78b9/sync?source=billing
```

maya: on it. running cache clear now.

sso-bot: audit: tenant t-78b9 SSO-claim mapping changed by billing-sync at 2026-03-17T08:17:05Z (job id sync-2234).

arjun: note: if SSO claim/role mappings changed recently we sometimes see entitlement-checks reject until role claims are re-parsed by the auth layer. good that we have the audit.

maya: cache clear returned 200. then I triggered sync.

maya: re-tested with customer's key at 08:34:01:
```
curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey cust_XXXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -v
> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{ "id": "gen-abc", "object": "generation" }
```

maya: customer confirmed on call they're unblocked now.

arjun: root cause notes: billing-sync updated plan + SSO claim mapping, but entitlement cache TTL/stale sync window meant runtime still enforced old plan gate; surfaced as 403 with reason=plan_gate which sometimes looks like auth error in UIs that map all 403s to \"invalid key\".

arjun: mitigation: reduce entitlement cache TTL for tenant update events, add a fast-path to re-parse SSO claims when billing job touches mapping, and emit clearer client error codes for plan gating (e.g., 403 + code=entitlement_required + doc link).

zach: filing follow-up with billing infra to add webhook to invalidate tenant cache on successful plan change job.

eng-oncall: logging follow-up: create incident note and attach customer repro + admin steps. tagging infra to track TTL tweak.

maya: closing loop with customer, they gave :+1:. thanks all.

maya: marking resolved and adding repro + fix steps to support KB: \"Why a seat upgrade might still return 403 (plan gating cache)\"
